checks: The original digest matches. Section 2, equations (6)–(13) of 159eef4ea58ca5da contain the same A, P, range of ε, arbitrary enclosing R, compact convex L, and ε/16 target.

Containments imply both excesses are nonnegative, so the Δ≥ε/16 branch closes immediately. In the other branch the outside triangles over the vertical, horizontal, and diagonal edges lie in R and are interior-disjoint from A. Their areas are respectively (1−ε)(−x)/2, (1−ε)(−y)/2, and (x+y−1)/2 when the corresponding supporting inequality is violated. Thus x,y≥−η and x+y≤1+2Δ for every point of R, with 2Δ≤η<ε/4.

The minimizing-sum vertex has both coordinates in [−η,ε+η]. Coordinate-maximizing vertices have q₁x≥1 and q₂y≥1, and satisfy |q₁y|,|q₂x|≤η. The sum bound 1+2Δ<2 makes q₁ and q₂ distinct, while their sums at least 1−η>ε distinguish both from q₀. This also handles ties in choosing maximizing or minimizing vertices.

The determinant lower bound expands to (1−2ε−3η)(1+η)>0. The left-side tests are exactly −(q₁x−ε)q₀y+q₁y(q₀x−ε)≥0 and −(q₂y−ε)q₀x+q₂x(q₀y−ε)≥0. Both denominators are positive. Each numerator has absolute value at most η(ε+η), giving q₀x+q₀y≤5ε²/4≤5ε/64<ε/2.

The lower edge of P has Euclidean length √2(2a−ε), and its distance from q₀ is (ε−q₀x−q₀y)/√2. Convexity puts their triangle inside L, with its interior on the opposite side of the support line from P. Dividing its area by four yields a strict bound above (2a−ε)ε/16≥31ε/256>ε/16. The argument does not assume L is triangular.

overlap.comparison: Its exterior-cone method bounds Hausdorff distance to a standard simplex under a volume budget, and labels vertices of a minimum container. It gives no strict side-of-cut conclusion for q₀ and no joint excess estimate for an arbitrary R and the prescribed P inside L.

readability: The q₁ and q₂ labels can be chosen to maximize the corresponding coordinates. Pending source a585520b0a2a14db gives the same A and P at d=2 but its coefficient c₂|T| is 1/128, weaker than the frozen 1/16.

summary: Every enclosing triangle either pays the stated endpoint area excess or has a vertex whose convex hull with the lower edge of P forces the stated scaled excess in L.
